If configuring this on servers causes issues, such as terminating users' remote sessions, and the organization has a policy in place that any other sessions on the servers, such as administrative console logons, are manually locked or logged off when unattended or not in use, this would be acceptable. ```

Smart-card removal locking extends this to CAC workflows.

### V-254460 · WN22-SO-000160 · CAT II: Windows Server 2022 setting Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always) must be configured to Enabled.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-254460r958908_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000423-GPOS-00187 |
| Topic | File Sharing (SMB) & Anonymous Access |
| CCI | CCI-002418, CCI-002421 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-8, SC-8 (1) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | SC-8, SC-8 (1) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | n/a |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |
| Server role | All servers (DC and member) |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** On this computer, setting Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always) must be configured to Enabled.

**Why it matters:** Computers on a network share files with each other using a system called SMB. This rule makes every file-sharing conversation carry a tamper-proof "seal" and stops strangers who haven't signed in from browsing the list of users and shared folders. It's like requiring visitors to sign in at the front desk before they can read the staff directory.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters | RequireSecuritySignature | REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always) | "Enabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters' -Name 'RequireSecuritySignature' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'RequireSecuritySignature'
```

Expected: RequireSecuritySignature = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters" /v "RequireSecuritySignature"
```

Expected: RequireSecuritySignature = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** Mostly Security Options: 'Microsoft network client/server: Digitally sign communications (always)' (RequireSecuritySignature), 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' (RestrictAnonymous), 'Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users', 'Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares', 'Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM'. SMBv1 is removed with 'Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol'. Check with 'Get-SmbServerConfiguration'.

**Operational impact:** Mandatory signing adds CPU overhead on high-throughput file servers (usually negligible on modern hardware) and can break very old clients and some NAS devices. Restricting anonymous access can affect legacy apps that rely on null sessions.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters\

Value Name: RequireSecuritySignature

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always) to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** The server message block (SMB) protocol provides the basis for many network operations. Digitally signed SMB packets aid in preventing man-in-the-middle attacks. If this policy is enabled, the SMB client will only communicate with an SMB server that performs SMB packet signing.

Satisfies: SRG-OS-000423-GPOS-00187, SRG-OS-000424-GPOS-00188

**Threat & control context:** SMB is the backbone of Windows file and administrative traffic and a principal lateral-movement channel. Unsigned SMB enables NTLM relay attacks. Anonymous (null session) access and SAM/share enumeration give unauthenticated attackers reconnaissance data such as user lists and group memberships. SMBv1 lacks modern protections and was the propagation vector for WannaCry and NotPetya. These settings support AC-3, AC-14 (actions without identification), SC-8 and CM-7.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay; T1135 Network Share Discovery; T1087 Account Discovery; T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** On this computer, setting Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (if server agrees) must be configured to Enabled.

**Why it matters:** Computers on a network share files with each other using a system called SMB. This rule makes every file-sharing conversation carry a tamper-proof "seal" and stops strangers who haven't signed in from browsing the list of users and shared folders. It's like requiring visitors to sign in at the front desk before they can read the staff directory.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|

Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters' -Name 'EnableSecuritySignature' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'EnableSecuritySignature'

```

Expected: EnableSecuritySignature = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** Mostly Security Options: 'Microsoft network client/server: Digitally sign communications (always)' (RequireSecuritySignature), 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' (RestrictAnonymous), 'Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users', 'Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares', 'Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM'. SMBv1 is removed with 'Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol'. Check with 'Get-SmbServerConfiguration'.

**Operational impact:** Mandatory signing adds CPU overhead on high-throughput file servers (usually negligible on modern hardware) and can break very old clients and some NAS devices. Restricting anonymous access can affect legacy apps that rely on null sessions.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Value Name: EnableSecuritySignature

Value Type: REG_DWORD

```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text

```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** The server message block (SMB) protocol provides the basis for many network operations. If this policy is enabled, the SMB client will request packet signing when communicating with an SMB server that is enabled or required to perform SMB packet signing.

Satisfies: SRG-OS-000423-GPOS-00187, SRG-OS-000424-GPOS-00188

**Threat & control context:** SMB is the backbone of Windows file and administrative traffic and a principal lateral-movement channel. Unsigned SMB enables NTLM relay attacks. Anonymous (null session) access and SAM/share enumeration give unauthenticated attackers reconnaissance data such as user lists and group memberships. **MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay; T1135 Network Share Discovery; T1087 Account Discovery; T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares

### V-254462 · WN22-SO-000180 · CAT II: Windows Server 2022 unencrypted passwords must not be sent to third-party Server Message Block (SMB) servers.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-254462r987796_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000074-GPOS-00042 |
| Topic | Password Age, History & Reuse, File Sharing (SMB) & Anonymous Access |
| CCI | CCI-000197 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-5 (1) (c) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | IA-5 (1) (c) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | IA-5 (1) (c) |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |
| Server role | All servers (DC and member) |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer's unencrypted passwords must not be sent to third-party Server Message Block (SMB) servers.

**Why it matters:** This makes people change passwords every so often and stops them from simply switching back to a password they used recently. If a password was quietly stolen, it eventually stops working, a bit like changing the locks periodically in case someone copied a key.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *SMB*: Server Message Block: the protocol Windows uses for file and printer sharing.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters | EnablePlainTextPassword | REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | Microsoft Network Client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers | "Disabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters' -Name 'EnablePlainTextPassword' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'EnablePlainTextPassword'
```

Expected: EnablePlainTextPassword = REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters" /v "EnablePlainTextPassword"
```

Expected: EnablePlainTextPassword = REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** Windows sets this in Account Policies >> Password Policy: 'Maximum password age', 'Minimum password age', 'Enforce password history'. Domain values come from the Default Domain Policy or PSOs.

**Also related (File Sharing (SMB) & Anonymous Access):** Mostly Security Options: 'Microsoft network client/server: Digitally sign communications (always)' (RequireSecuritySignature), 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' (RestrictAnonymous), 'Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users', 'Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares', 'Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM'. SMBv1 is removed with 'Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol'. Check with 'Get-SmbServerConfiguration'.

**Operational impact:** Changing login.defs does not retroactively update existing accounts, so remember to run chage for current users. Exclude non-interactive service accounts from expiry only through a documented exception (or use gMSAs on Windows).

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive:  HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path:  \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters\

Value Name:  EnablePlainTextPassword

Value Type:  REG_DWORD
Value:  0x00000000 (0)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> Microsoft Network Client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers to "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Some non-Microsoft SMB servers only support unencrypted (plain-text) password authentication. Sending plain-text passwords across the network when authenticating to an SMB server reduces the overall security of the environment. Check with the vendor of the SMB server to determine if there is a way to support encrypted password authentication.

**Threat & control context:** Maximum age bounds the useful lifetime of a compromised credential. Minimum age plus history prevent users from cycling straight back to a known password, which would defeat the history check (IA-5(1)(d)/(e)). The trend in current guidance is to prefer event-driven rotation (on suspected compromise) over periodic rotation, but the DoD baseline values remain enforceable requirements.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1078 Valid Accounts; T1110.004 Brute Force: Credential Stuffing; T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay; T1135 Network Share Discovery; T1087 Account Discovery; T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000197**: For password-based authentication, transmit passwords only over cryptographically-protected channels.  
  Rev 5: IA-5 (1) (c) · Rev 4: IA-5 (1) (c) · Rev 3: IA-5 (1) (c)

### V-254470 · WN22-SO-000260 · CAT II: Windows Server 2022 services using Local System that use Negotiate when reverting to NTLM authentication must use the computer identity instead of authenticating anonymously.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-254470r991589_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000480-GPOS-00227 |
| Topic | Windows Authentication Protocols (NTLM, Kerberos, LSA), File Sharing (SMB) & Anonymous Access |
| CCI | CCI-000366 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | CM-6 b |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |
| Server role | All servers (DC and member) |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer's services using Local System that use Negotiate when reverting to NTLM authentication must use the computer identity instead of authenticating anonymously.

**Why it matters:** When you log into a Windows network, your computer and the server trade secret "handshakes" to prove who you are. Older handshakes are easy for attackers to fake or steal. This rule switches off the old, weak handshakes and protects the part of memory where Windows keeps your sign-in secrets, like retiring an old ID badge design that was easy to forge.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *NTLM / LAN Manager*: Older Windows sign-in methods that are weaker than modern Kerberos.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA | UseMachineId | REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM | "Enabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA' -Name 'UseMachineId' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'UseMachineId'
```

Expected: UseMachineId = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA" /v "UseMachineId"
```

Expected: UseMachineId = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** Most of these are Security Options under Local Policies, plus MS Security Guide templates (SecGuide.admx shipped with the STIG GPO package). Key settings include 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' (LmCompatibilityLevel = 5), 'Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos', 'Minimum session security for NTLM SSP', WDigest 'UseLogonCredential' = 0, and Credential Guard via Device Guard >> 'Turn On Virtualization Based Security'. Verify with 'gpresult /h' or the registry paths shown in the check.

**Also related (File Sharing (SMB) & Anonymous Access):** Mostly Security Options: 'Microsoft network client/server: Digitally sign communications (always)' (RequireSecuritySignature), 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' (RestrictAnonymous), 'Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users', 'Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares', 'Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM'. SMBv1 is removed with 'Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol'. Check with 'Get-SmbServerConfiguration'.

**Operational impact:** Enforcing NTLMv2-only or AES-only Kerberos can break legacy appliances, older NAS devices, multifunction printers and non-Windows clients. Run NTLM and Kerberos auditing (event IDs 4624/4776/4768/4769) first to inventory dependencies. Credential Guard is incompatible with some VPN clients and with unconstrained delegation.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA\

Value Name: UseMachineId

Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Services using Local System that use Negotiate when reverting to NTLM authentication may gain unauthorized access if allowed to authenticate anonymously versus using the computer identity.

**Threat & control context:** Windows authentication protocols are central to most domain compromise chains. Legacy LM/NTLMv1 responses can be cracked or relayed. WDigest leaves cleartext passwords in LSASS memory. Weak Kerberos encryption types (RC4/DES) enable Kerberoasting and downgrade attacks. Credential Guard and LSA protection (RunAsPPL) isolate secrets from credential-dumping tools. These settings implement IA-2(8) (replay resistance), IA-5(1)(c), SC-8 and SC-23 (session authenticity). Validate the domain-wide impact with NTLM auditing before enforcing restrictions.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1003.001 OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory; T1550.002 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash; T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay; T1558 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets; T1135 Network Share Discovery; T1087 Account Discovery; T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | Network security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests | this computer to use online identities to "Disabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA\pku2u' -Name 'AllowOnlineID' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'AllowOnlineID'
```

Expected: AllowOnlineID = REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA\pku2u" /v "AllowOnlineID"
```

Expected: AllowOnlineID = REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** Most of these are Security Options under Local Policies, plus MS Security Guide templates (SecGuide.admx shipped with the STIG GPO package). Key settings include 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' (LmCompatibilityLevel = 5), 'Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos', 'Minimum session security for NTLM SSP', WDigest 'UseLogonCredential' = 0, and Credential Guard via Device Guard >> 'Turn On Virtualization Based Security'. Verify with 'gpresult /h' or the registry paths shown in the check.

**Also related (Telemetry, Cloud & Consumer Features):** On Windows these are mostly Administrative Templates under Windows Components (Data Collection and Preview Builds, Cloud Content, Search, Store, OneDrive, Windows Error Reporting, App Privacy) and the Microsoft Edge templates. Verify the registry values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\... as shown in each check.

**Operational impact:** Enforcing NTLMv2-only or AES-only Kerberos can break legacy appliances, older NAS devices, multifunction printers and non-Windows clients. Run NTLM and Kerberos auditing (event IDs 4624/4776/4768/4769) first to inventory dependencies. Credential Guard is incompatible with some VPN clients and with unconstrained delegation.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA\pku2u\

Value Name: AllowOnlineID

Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000000 (0)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> Network security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities to "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** PKU2U is a peer-to-peer authentication protocol. This setting prevents online identities from authenticating to domain-joined systems. Authentication will be centrally managed with Windows user accounts.

**Threat & control context:** Windows authentication protocols are central to most domain compromise chains. Legacy LM/NTLMv1 responses can be cracked or relayed. WDigest leaves cleartext passwords in LSASS memory. Weak Kerberos encryption types (RC4/DES) enable Kerberoasting and downgrade attacks. Credential Guard and LSA protection (RunAsPPL) isolate secrets from credential-dumping tools. These settings implement IA-2(8) (replay resistance), IA-5(1)(c), SC-8 and SC-23 (session authenticity). Validate the domain-wide impact with NTLM auditing before enforcing restrictions.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1003.001 OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory; T1550.002 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash; T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay; T1558 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets; T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service; T1213 Data from Information Repositories

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.

Key settings include 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' (LmCompatibilityLevel = 5), 'Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos', 'Minimum session security for NTLM SSP', WDigest 'UseLogonCredential' = 0, and Credential Guard via Device Guard >> 'Turn On Virtualization Based Security'. Verify with 'gpresult /h' or the registry paths shown in the check.

**Operational impact:** Enforcing NTLMv2-only or AES-only Kerberos can break legacy appliances, older NAS devices, multifunction printers and non-Windows clients. Run NTLM and Kerberos auditing (event IDs 4624/4776/4768/4769) first to inventory dependencies. Credential Guard is incompatible with some VPN clients and with unconstrained delegation.

Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos to "Enabled" with only the following selected:

AES128_HMAC_SHA1
AES256_HMAC_SHA1

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Certain encryption types are no longer considered secure. The DES and RC4 encryption suites must not be used for Kerberos encryption.

WDigest leaves cleartext passwords in LSASS memory. Weak Kerberos encryption types (RC4/DES) enable Kerberoasting and downgrade attacks. ### V-254474 · WN22-SO-000300 · CAT I: Windows Server 2022 must be configured to prevent the storage of the LAN Manager hash of passwords.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-254474r1051107_rule` |
| Severity | CAT I (high) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000073-GPOS-00041 |
| Topic | Credential Storage & Password Hashing |
| CCI | CCI-004062, CCI-000196 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-5 (1) (d) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | IA-5 (1) (c) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | IA-5 (1) (c) |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |
| Server role | All servers (DC and member) |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer must be configured to prevent the storage of the LAN Manager hash of passwords.

**Why it matters:** Computers shouldn't store your actual password. Instead they store a scrambled "fingerprint" of it that can't be turned back into the password. This rule makes sure that fingerprint is created with a strong method, so that even if someone steals the file, they can't easily work out everyone's passwords.

**How important is it?** High priority (CAT I): If this setting is wrong, an attacker could directly and immediately gain access, take control, or cause serious damage. These are fixed first.

**Key terms:**
- *NTLM / LAN Manager*: Older Windows sign-in methods that are weaker than modern Kerberos.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa | NoLMHash | REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change | "Enabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name 'NoLMHash' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'NoLMHash'
```

Expected: NoLMHash = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v "NoLMHash"
```

Expected: NoLMHash = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** Relevant Windows settings include 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change' (NoLMHash), 'Store passwords using reversible encryption' (Disabled), and 'Interactive logon: Number of previous logons to cache' (CachedLogonsCount).

**Operational impact:** Reducing cached logons can prevent laptop users from signing in when they are off the network. Disabling LM hashes affects only very old clients (pre-Windows 2000 era).

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\

Value Name: NoLMHash

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** The LAN Manager hash uses a weak encryption algorithm and there are several tools available that use this hash to retrieve account passwords. This setting controls whether a LAN Manager hash of the password is stored in the SAM the next time the password is changed.

**Threat & control context:** When a host is compromised, stored credential material is the attacker's path to lateral movement. Weak or reversible storage (LM hashes, reversible encryption, low-iteration hashes, excessive cached domain logons) turns a single compromise into credential recovery for many accounts. IA-5(1)(c) requires that only cryptographically protected passwords be stored and transmitted. Strong salted, iterated hashing such as SHA-512 crypt with sufficient rounds increases offline cracking cost.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1003 OS Credential Dumping; T1110.002 Brute Force: Password Cracking; T1552 Unsecured Credentials

**Severity rationale:** CAT I: any vulnerability whose exploitation will directly and immediately result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-004062**: For password-based authentication, store passwords using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash.  
  Rev 5: IA-5 (1) (d) · Rev 4: n/a · Rev 3: n/a
- **CCI-000196**: The information system, for password-based authentication, stores only cryptographically-protected passwords.  
  Rev 5: n/a · Rev 4: IA-5 (1) (c) · Rev 3: IA-5 (1) (c)

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer must be configured to at least negotiate signing for LDAP client signing.

**Why it matters:** In an organization, a few central servers (domain controllers) keep the master list of every user, password and permission. This rule adds extra protection to those servers and the conversations other computers have with them. It's like guarding the room that holds the master key cabinet more tightly than any other room in the building.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *LDAP*: A protocol for looking up users and groups in a central directory.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LDAP | LDAPClientIntegrity | REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | Network security: LDAP client signing requirements | "Negotiate signing" at a minimum |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LDAP' -Name 'LDAPClientIntegrity' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'LDAPClientIntegrity'
```

Expected: LDAPClientIntegrity = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LDAP" /v "LDAPClientIntegrity"
```

Expected: LDAPClientIntegrity = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** On Windows, the relevant Security Options include 'Domain controller: LDAP server signing requirements' (Require signing), 'Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always)' and 'Domain member: Maximum machine account password age' (30 days). DC-specific checks review permissions on NTDS (%SystemRoot%\NTDS), SYSVOL and GPOs, and AD object auditing (SACLs). Use 'dcdiag', 'repadmin /showrepl' and ADSI Edit or 'Get-Acl AD:' to verify.

**Also related (File Sharing (SMB) & Anonymous Access):** Mostly Security Options: 'Microsoft network client/server: Digitally sign communications (always)' (RequireSecuritySignature), 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' (RestrictAnonymous), 'Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users', 'Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares', 'Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM'. SMBv1 is removed with 'Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol'. Check with 'Get-SmbServerConfiguration'.

**Operational impact:** Enforcing LDAP signing or channel binding breaks clients and appliances that use simple binds over unsigned LDAP. Check Directory Service event 2889 to find them before enforcing.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LDAP\

Value Name: LDAPClientIntegrity

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> Network security: LDAP client signing requirements to "Negotiate signing" at a minimum.
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** This setting controls the signing requirements for LDAP clients. This must be set to "Negotiate signing" or "Require signing", depending on the environment and type of LDAP server in use.

**Threat & control context:** Domain controllers hold the keys to every domain identity, so DC compromise is total enterprise compromise. Requirements cover LDAP signing and channel binding (anti-relay), secure-channel signing and sealing, machine-account password rotation, protection of NTDS/SYSVOL/GPO permissions, restricting who can administer and log on to DCs, and directory auditing. These implement AC-3, AC-6, SC-8, SC-23 and AU-2 for the identity tier. Assess them alongside the administrative tiering model.

Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0' -Name 'NTLMMinClientSec' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'NTLMMinClientSec'
```

Expected: NTLMMinClientSec = REG_DWORD = 0x20080000 (537395200). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0" /v "NTLMMinClientSec"
```

Expected: NTLMMinClientSec = REG_DWORD = 0x20080000 (537395200). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** On Windows, 'System cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing' (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\FIPSAlgorithmPolicy\Enabled) restricts Schannel and CNG to FIPS-approved algorithms. Related settings cover Kerberos encryption types and NTLM session security.

**Also related (Windows Authentication Protocols (NTLM, Kerberos, LSA)):** Most of these are Security Options under Local Policies, plus MS Security Guide templates (SecGuide.admx shipped with the STIG GPO package). Key settings include 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' (LmCompatibilityLevel = 5), 'Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos', 'Minimum session security for NTLM SSP', WDigest 'UseLogonCredential' = 0, and Credential Guard via Device Guard >> 'Turn On Virtualization Based Security'. Verify with 'gpresult /h' or the registry paths shown in the check.

**Operational impact:** Enabling FIPS mode can break applications that use non-approved algorithms (MD5 for non-security checksums, older .NET code, legacy VPN or RDP clients). Test interoperating systems and line-of-business applications before rollout.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0\

Value Name: NTLMMinClientSec

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x20080000 (537395200)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients to "Require NTLMv2 session security" and "Require 128-bit encryption" (all options selected).
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Microsoft has implemented a variety of security support providers for use with Remote Procedure Call (RPC) sessions. All of the options must be enabled to ensure the maximum security level.

**Threat & control context:** Federal systems must use FIPS 140-validated cryptographic modules (SC-13). Weak or legacy algorithms (MD5, SHA-1 MACs, CBC-mode ciphers, RC4, DES/3DES, small DH groups) enable downgrade, decryption or forgery attacks against data in transit (SC-8, SC-8(1)). The control is only as strong as its weakest negotiated option, so assessors look at the full allowed list, not just the preferred algorithm. Note that FIPS mode validates the module, not the protocol configuration, so both must be checked.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1040 Network Sniffing; T1557 Adversary-in-the-Middle; T1600 Weaken Encryption; T1003.001 OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory; T1550.002 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash; T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay; T1558 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

### V-254479 · WN22-SO-000350 · CAT II: Windows Server 2022 users must be required to enter a password to access private keys stored on the computer.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-254479r958450_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000067-GPOS-00035 |
| Topic | Credential Storage & Password Hashing |
| CCI | CCI-000186 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-5 (2) (a) (1) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | IA-5 (2) (b) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | IA-5 (2) |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |
| Server role | All servers (DC and member) |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer's users must be required to enter a password to access private keys stored on the computer.

**Why it matters:** Computers shouldn't store your actual password. Instead they store a scrambled "fingerprint" of it that can't be turned back into the password. This rule makes sure that fingerprint is created with a strong method, so that even if someone steals the file, they can't easily work out everyone's passwords.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Cryptography | ForceKeyProtection | REG_DWORD = 0x00000002 (2) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | System cryptography: Force strong key protection for user keys stored on the computer | "User must enter a password each time they use a key" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Cryptography' -Name 'ForceKeyProtection' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'ForceKeyProtection'
```

Expected: ForceKeyProtection = REG_DWORD = 0x00000002 (2). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Cryptography" /v "ForceKeyProtection"
```

Expected: ForceKeyProtection = REG_DWORD = 0x00000002 (2). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** Relevant Windows settings include 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change' (NoLMHash), 'Store passwords using reversible encryption' (Disabled), and 'Interactive logon: Number of previous logons to cache' (CachedLogonsCount).

**Operational impact:** Reducing cached logons can prevent laptop users from signing in when they are off the network. Disabling LM hashes affects only very old clients (pre-Windows 2000 era).

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive:  HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path:  \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Cryptography\

Value Name:  ForceKeyProtection

Type:  REG_DWORD
Value:  0x00000002 (2)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> System cryptography: Force strong key protection for user keys stored on the computer to "User must enter a password each time they use a key".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** If the private key is discovered, an attacker can use the key to authenticate as an authorized user and gain access to the network infrastructure.

The cornerstone of the PKI is the private key used to encrypt or digitally sign information.

If the private key is stolen, this will lead to the compromise of the authentication and nonrepudiation gained through PKI because the attacker can use the private key to digitally sign documents and pretend to be the authorized user.

Both the holders of a digital certificate and the issuing authority must protect the computers, storage devices, or whatever they use to keep the private keys.

**Threat & control context:** When a host is compromised, stored credential material is the attacker's path to lateral movement. Weak or reversible storage (LM hashes, reversible encryption, low-iteration hashes, excessive cached domain logons) turns a single compromise into credential recovery for many accounts. IA-5(1)(c) requires that only cryptographically protected passwords be stored and transmitted. Strong salted, iterated hashing such as SHA-512 crypt with sufficient rounds increases offline cracking cost.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1003 OS Credential Dumping; T1110.002 Brute Force: Password Cracking; T1552 Unsecured Credentials

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000186**: For public key-based authentication, enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key.  
  Rev 5: IA-5 (2) (a) (1) · Rev 4: IA-5 (2) (b) · Rev 3: IA-5 (2)

### V-254481 · WN22-SO-000370 · CAT III: Windows Server 2022 default permissions of global system objects must be strengthened.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-254481r991589_rule` |
| Severity | CAT III (low) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000480-GPOS-00227 |

| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | CM-6 b |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |
| Server role | All servers (DC and member) |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer's default permissions of global system objects must be strengthened.

**Why it matters:** Every file on a computer has a label saying who owns it and who can read or change it. This rule makes sure sensitive files, such as the list of password fingerprints or system settings, can only be touched by the right people. It's like keeping personnel files in a locked HR cabinet rather than on the break-room table.

**How important is it?** Low priority (CAT III): This setting adds an extra layer of protection. A gap here on its own is less likely to cause harm, but it weakens the overall defenses.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager | ProtectionMode | REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g., Symbolic Links) | "Enabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager' -Name 'ProtectionMode' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'ProtectionMode'
```

Expected: ProtectionMode = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager" /v "ProtectionMode"
```

Expected: ProtectionMode = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** On Windows, check NTFS ACLs with 'icacls <path>' or 'Get-Acl'. The STIG specifies baseline ACLs for system folders, registry hives and event logs. Don't broaden the default ACLs on %SystemRoot%, Program Files or HKLM\SECURITY.

**Operational impact:** Tightening permissions can break applications that read their configuration as a non-root user. Prefer group-based access over loosening the mode, and re-check after package updates, which can reset modes.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\

Value Name: ProtectionMode

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g., Symbolic Links) to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Windows systems maintain a global list of shared system resources such as DOS device names, mutexes, and semaphores. Each type of object is created with a default Discretionary Access Control List (DACL) that specifies who can access the objects with what permissions. When this policy is enabled, the default DACL is stronger, allowing nonadministrative users to read shared objects but not to modify shared objects they did not create.

**Threat & control context:** Permissive ownership or modes on credentials (shadow, SSH host keys), libraries, system binaries, cron and boot configuration, and log files allow tampering, credential theft and execution-flow hijacking. This is AC-3 / AC-6 least privilege applied at the file-system layer, plus CM-5(6) (privilege to change software libraries). Unowned files and world-writable directories without the sticky bit are common persistence and escalation footholds.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1222 File and Directory Permissions Modification; T1574 Hijack Execution Flow; T1548.001 Abuse Elevation Control: Setuid and Setgid

**Severity rationale:** CAT III: any vulnerability whose existence degrades measures to protect against loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

### V-254482 · WN22-SO-000380 · CAT II: Windows Server 2022 User Account Control (UAC) approval mode for the built-in Administrator must be enabled.

| Field | Value |

| Rule ID | `SV-254482r1051108_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000373-GPOS-00156 |
| Topic | Built-in & Privileged Account Hardening, Privilege Elevation (UAC / sudo) |
| CCI | CCI-002038 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-11 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | IA-11 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | n/a |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |
| Server role | All servers (DC and member) |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer's User Account Control (UAC) approval mode for the built-in Administrator must be enabled.

**Why it matters:** Every computer comes with a few built-in "master" accounts whose names everyone knows. This rule makes those accounts harder to abuse, for example by not letting anyone log in directly as the master account and never allowing accounts with no password. It's like not leaving the master key labelled "MASTER KEY" hanging by the front door.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *UAC*: User Account Control: the Windows pop-up that asks for confirmation before something makes system-wide changes.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System | FilterAdministratorToken | REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account | "Enabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System' -Name 'FilterAdministratorToken' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'FilterAdministratorToken'
```

Expected: FilterAdministratorToken = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v "FilterAdministratorToken"
```

Expected: FilterAdministratorToken = REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** On Windows these are Security Options ('Accounts: Rename administrator account', 'Accounts: Guest account status', 'Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only') plus LAPS for unique, rotated local administrator passwords.

**Also related (Privilege Elevation (UAC / sudo)):** UAC settings are Security Options named 'User Account Control: ...' (registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System: EnableLUA, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin, ConsentPromptBehaviorUser, FilterAdministratorToken, EnableInstallerDetection, EnableSecureUIAPaths, EnableVirtualization).

**Operational impact:** Make sure at least one named administrator account with sudo or admin rights works before disabling root or Administrator logon paths. Renaming the built-in Administrator can break scripts that reference it by name.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
UAC requirements are NA for Server Core installations (this is the default installation option for Windows Server 2022 versus Server with Desktop Experience).

If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\

Value Name: FilterAdministratorToken

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** UAC is a security mechanism for limiting the elevation of privileges, including administrative accounts, unless authorized. This setting configures the built-in Administrator account so that it runs in Admin Approval Mode.

Satisfies: SRG-OS-000373-GPOS-00156, SRG-OS-000373-GPOS-00157

**Threat & control context:** Well-known accounts (root, Administrator, Guest) are guaranteed to exist with predictable names, which makes them ideal targets. Blocking direct logon forces attribution through named accounts (IA-2, AC-6(2)). Removing empty-password acceptance eliminates trivial access, and unique local admin passwords (LAPS) break pass-the-hash lateral movement across a fleet. Assess the effective result across every access path: console, SSH, RDP and network logon.

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer's UIAccess applications must not be allowed to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop.

**Why it matters:** Even administrators work day-to-day without full power, and the system asks them to confirm, often by re-entering a password, before doing anything that could change important settings. That way, a harmful program can't quietly use admin power behind their back. It's like a bank requiring a second signature for large withdrawals.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *UAC*: User Account Control: the Windows pop-up that asks for confirmation before something makes system-wide changes.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System | EnableUIADesktopToggle | REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options | User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop | "Disabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System' -Name 'EnableUIADesktopToggle' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'EnableUIADesktopToggle'
```

Expected: EnableUIADesktopToggle = REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v "EnableUIADesktopToggle"
```

Expected: EnableUIADesktopToggle = REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** UAC settings are Security Options named 'User Account Control: ...' (registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System: EnableLUA, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin, ConsentPromptBehaviorUser, FilterAdministratorToken, EnableInstallerDetection, EnableSecureUIAPaths, EnableVirtualization).

**Operational impact:** Turning off password-less sudo affects automation such as Ansible and cron jobs. Use dedicated automation accounts with tightly scoped command lists and documented exceptions. Disabling UAC (EnableLUA = 0) is not acceptable and also breaks Store/UWP apps.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
UAC requirements are NA for Server Core installations (this is the default installation option for Windows Server 2022 versus Server with Desktop Experience).

If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\

Value Name: EnableUIADesktopToggle

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000000 (0)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop to "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** User Account Control (UAC) is a security mechanism for limiting the elevation of privileges, including administrative accounts, unless authorized. This setting prevents User Interface Accessibility programs from disabling the secure desktop for elevation prompts.

**Threat & control context:** Elevation controls make privilege use deliberate, authenticated and auditable (AC-6(1)/(2)/(9)/(10), IA-11 re-authentication). UAC's secure-desktop prompt resists UI spoofing and input injection by malware running in the user's session. sudo restrictions (no NOPASSWD, no '!authenticate', short timestamp_timeout, no blanket ALL grants) prevent silent escalation by any process running as an admin user. Every elevation event should produce an audit record.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1548.002 Abuse Elevation Control: Bypass UAC; T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control: Sudo and Sudo Caching; T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-001084**: Isolate security functions from nonsecurity functions.  
  Rev 5: SC-3 · Rev 4: SC-3 · Rev 3: SC-3

(registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System: EnableLUA, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin, ConsentPromptBehaviorUser, FilterAdministratorToken, EnableInstallerDetection, EnableSecureUIAPaths, EnableVirtualization).

**Operational impact:** Turning off password-less sudo affects automation such as Ansible and cron jobs. Use dedicated automation accounts with tightly scoped command lists and documented exceptions. Disabling UAC (EnableLUA = 0) is not acceptable and also breaks Store/UWP apps.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
UAC requirements are NA for Server Core installations (this is the default installation option for Windows Server 2022 versus Server with Desktop Experience).

If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\

Value Name: EnableLUA

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> Security Options >> User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** UAC is a security mechanism for limiting the elevation of privileges, including administrative accounts, unless authorized. This setting enables UAC.

Satisfies: SRG-OS-000373-GPOS-00156, SRG-OS-000373-GPOS-00157

**Threat & control context:** Elevation controls make privilege use deliberate, authenticated and auditable (AC-6(1)/(2)/(9)/(10), IA-11 re-authentication). UAC's secure-desktop prompt resists UI spoofing and input injection by malware running in the user's session. sudo restrictions (no NOPASSWD, no '!authenticate', short timestamp_timeout, no blanket ALL grants) prevent silent escalation by any process running as an admin user. Every elevation event should produce an audit record.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1548.002 Abuse Elevation Control: Bypass UAC; T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control: Sudo and Sudo Caching; T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-002038**: The organization requires users to reauthenticate upon organization-defined circumstances or situations requiring reauthentication.  
  Rev 5: IA-11 · Rev 4: IA-11 · Rev 3: n/a

### V-254490 · WN22-UC-000010 · CAT II: Windows Server 2022 must preserve zone information when saving attachments.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-254490r1260035_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |

| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-6 b |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer must preserve zone information when saving attachments.

**Why it matters:** Modern computers like to "phone home", sending usage data to the manufacturer, syncing to personal cloud accounts, or showing ads and suggestions. This rule turns those features off or down so government information stays inside the government's systems, like not letting a delivery driver wander through the office and take notes.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Attachments | SaveZoneInformation | REG_DWORD = 0x00000002 (2) (or if the Value Name does not exist) |
| Group Policy | User Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Attachment Manager | Do not preserve zone information in file attachments | "Not Configured" or "Disabled" |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Attachments' -Name 'SaveZoneInformation' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'SaveZoneInformation'
```

Expected: SaveZoneInformation = REG_DWORD = 0x00000002 (2) (or if the Value Name does not exist). A missing value or path is a finding.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
reg query "HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Attachments" /v "SaveZoneInformation"
```

Expected: SaveZoneInformation = REG_DWORD = 0x00000002 (2) (or if the Value Name does not exist). A missing value or path is a finding.

**How it works:** On Windows these are mostly Administrative Templates under Windows Components (Data Collection and Preview Builds, Cloud Content, Search, Store, OneDrive, Windows Error Reporting, App Privacy) and the Microsoft Edge templates. Verify the registry values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\... as shown in each check.

**Operational impact:** Users lose consumer conveniences such as Store apps, Microsoft-account sign-in and web results in search. Enterprise management may need a minimum telemetry level (e.g. for Windows Update for Business reports), so align the value with the STIG's allowed options.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
Note: This Check must be performed for each interactive user profile on the system.

The default behavior is for Windows to mark file attachments with their zone information.

If the registry Value Name below does not exist, this is not a finding.

If it exists and is configured with a value of "2", this is not a finding.

If it exists and is configured with a value of "1", this is a finding.

Registry Hive: HKEY_CURRENT_USER
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Attachments\

Value Name: SaveZoneInformation

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000002 (2) (or if the Value Name does not exist)

Note: This requirement is applicable to profiles for interactive logins. It is not applicable for Service accounts.

To determine the system's enabled user profiles:
Run "PowerShell" as an administrator.

Execute the following command:
Get-LocalUser | Where-Object {$_.Enabled -eq $true}
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
The default behavior is for Windows to mark file attachments with their zone information.

If this needs to be corrected, for each user profile on the system configure the policy value for User Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Attachment Manager >> Do not preserve zone information in file attachments to "Not Configured" or "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Attachments from outside sources may contain malicious code. Preserving zone of origin (internet, intranet, local, restricted) information on file attachments allows Windows to determine risk.

**Threat & control context:** Consumer-oriented and cloud-connected features can move government data (documents, typed input, location, diagnostic dumps containing memory contents) to vendor or third-party services outside the authorization boundary. Disabling or restricting them supports SC-7 (boundary protection), AC-20 (use of external systems), CM-7 and privacy controls, and removes unvetted functionality from the baseline.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service; T1213 Data from Information Repositories

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

### V-254491 · WN22-UR-000010 · CAT II: Windows Server 2022 Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller user right must not be assigned to any groups or accounts.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-254491r958726_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000324-GPOS-00125 |
| Topic | Windows User Rights Assignment, Credential Storage & Password Hashing |
| CCI | CCI-002235 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-6 (10) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | AC-6 (10) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | n/a |
| Implemented via | Group Policy |
| Server role | All servers (DC and member) |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer's Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller user right must not be assigned to any groups or accounts.

**Why it matters:** Windows has a list of special powers, such as "shut down the computer", "look inside other programs' memory" or "log in remotely", and decides which accounts get each one. This rule makes sure only the right people, usually administrators, hold the powerful ones. It's like a hospital where only surgeons are allowed into the operating room.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> User Rights Assignment | Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller | No accounts or groups (defined, blank) |

**Command-line validation:**

*PowerShell* (generated from the setting)

```text
secedit /export /cfg "$env:TEMP\secpol.inf" /areas USER_RIGHTS /quiet; Select-String -Path "$env:TEMP\secpol.inf" -Pattern '^SeTrustedCredManAccessPrivilege\b'
```

Expected: SeTrustedCredManAccessPrivilege lists only: No accounts or groups (defined, blank). Accounts appear as names or SIDs (*S-1-5-32-544 = Administrators, *S-1-5-32-546 = Guests, *S-1-5-11 = Authenticated Users, *S-1-5-113 = Local account). No line at all means no one holds the right. Run elevated.

*CMD* (generated from the setting)

```text
secedit /export /cfg %TEMP%\secpol.inf /areas USER_RIGHTS /quiet && findstr /i /b "SeTrustedCredManAccessPrivilege" %TEMP%\secpol.inf
```

Expected: SeTrustedCredManAccessPrivilege lists only: No accounts or groups (defined, blank). Accounts appear as names or SIDs (*S-1-5-32-544 = Administrators, *S-1-5-32-546 = Guests, *S-1-5-11 = Authenticated Users, *S-1-5-113 = Local account). No line at all means no one holds the right. Run elevated.

**How it works:** Configured at Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> User Rights Assignment. These are not registry values: they are stored in the local security database and applied from GptTmpl.inf in a GPO. Review the effective assignment with 'secedit /export /cfg c:\temp\secpol.inf /areas USER_RIGHTS' or the Local Security Policy console. An empty but defined setting means 'no one'.

**Also related (Credential Storage & Password Hashing):** Relevant Windows settings include 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change' (NoLMHash), 'Store passwords using reversible encryption' (Disabled), and 'Interactive logon: Number of previous logons to cache' (CachedLogonsCount).

**Operational impact:** Removing service accounts from rights such as 'Log on as a service' or 'Impersonate a client after authentication' can stop applications (SQL Server, IIS app pools, backup agents). Document required application accounts as approved exceptions before enforcing.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
Verify the effective setting in Local Group Policy Editor.

Run "gpedit.msc".

Navigate to Local Computer Policy >> Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> User Rights Assignment.

If any accounts or groups are granted the "Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller" user right, this is a finding.

For server core installations, run the following command:

Secedit /Export /Areas User_Rights /cfg c:\path\filename.txt

Review the text file.

If any SIDs are granted the "SeTrustedCredManAccessPrivilege" user right, this is a finding.
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> User Rights Assignment >> Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller to be defined but containing no entries (blank).
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Inappropriate granting of user rights can provide system, administrative, and other high-level capabilities.

Accounts with the "Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller" user right may be able to retrieve the credentials of other accounts from Credential Manager.

**Threat & control context:** User rights (privileges) such as SeDebugPrivilege, SeImpersonatePrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, SeTcbPrivilege and SeLoadDriverPrivilege each give a direct path to SYSTEM-level compromise or credential theft. Logon rights (network, interactive, RDP, batch, service) define which accounts can authenticate through which channel. Enforcing least privilege here implements AC-6 / AC-6(10) and limits blast radius when a lower-privileged account is compromised. Pay particular attention to 'Deny' rights for privileged domain accounts on lower-tier systems, which enforce an administrative tiering model.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1134 Access Token Manipulation; T1003 OS Credential Dumping; T1078 Valid Accounts; T1110.002 Brute Force: Password Cracking; T1552 Unsecured Credentials

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-002235**: Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.  
  Rev 5: AC-6 (10) · Rev 4: AC-6 (10) · Rev 3: n/a

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Windows Settings >> Security Settings >> Local Policies >> User Rights Assignment >> Allow log on locally to include only the following accounts or groups:

- Administrators
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Inappropriate granting of user rights can provide system, administrative, and other high-level capabilities.

Accounts with the "Allow log on locally" user right can log on interactively to a system.

**Threat & control context:** User rights (privileges) such as SeDebugPrivilege, SeImpersonatePrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, SeTcbPrivilege and SeLoadDriverPrivilege each give a direct path to SYSTEM-level compromise or credential theft. Logon rights (network, interactive, RDP, batch, service) define which accounts can authenticate through which channel. Enforcing least privilege here implements AC-6 / AC-6(10) and limits blast radius when a lower-privileged account is compromised. Pay particular attention to 'Deny' rights for privileged domain accounts on lower-tier systems, which enforce an administrative tiering model.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1134 Access Token Manipulation; T1003 OS Credential Dumping; T1078 Valid Accounts

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.
